newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Luismin sees silver prices rising in '98.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Luismin sees silver prices rising in '98.

text.p: Industrias Luismin, the mining arm of conglomerate Sanluis Corporacion, sees silver prices rising to $5.50 to $6.00 an ounce next year, the company's director general said Thursday.
In an interview with Reuters, Eduardo Luna said low world stock levels should soon begin to affect prices.
"Prices have to react to the situation," he added. "Quite easily, we could see prices in the $5.50 to $6.00 range."

Luna said Luismin's silver price outlook reflected the company's hedging strategies. "We have almost no hedging in silver," Luna said. All the company's forecast gold output was hedged for 1998 and 1999.
World silver prices are currently hovering a little higher than $4.70.
